name: Fisetin
short: Small studies only: no adverse effects noted in 10 healthy adults over 50 (6 months, no control group); none reported in 15 volunteers given single doses. Other trial abstracts give no safety data.
text: Human safety data on fisetin come only from small studies. In a 6-month pilot study without a control group in 10 healthy adults over 50, who took fisetin daily for one week each month, no adverse effects were noted; biological-age test results rose in five participants, fell in four and did not change in one, and the authors advise against taking it as an anti-ageing agent until larger studies are done. In a randomised, double-blind crossover study in 15 healthy volunteers given single doses by mouth of plain fisetin and of an encapsulated fisetin formulation, no adverse events were reported. Randomised trials of fisetin in 37 people with colorectal cancer having chemotherapy, in people with ischaemic stroke who were also given recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA), and in 60 and 44 men with obesity give no adverse-event data in their abstracts, and the stroke trial's abstract gives no bleeding data. A 2026 report describes the design of a placebo-controlled phase 2 trial of fisetin taken by mouth in 88 breast cancer survivors, with no results yet. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
